Yet their rushed development has outpaced critical oversight, leaving key workflow decisions dangerously unscrutinized. We present a much-needed systematic analysis of open-source AI scientist systems, investigating four primary pitfalls: inappropriate benchmark selection, data leakage, metric misuse, and post hoc selection bias. Through controlled experiments that isolate each pitfall, we find systematic vulnerabilities across two representative open-source systems. Crucially, we find that these flaws are largely invisible at the level of the final manuscript, suggesting that current manuscript-centric peer review paradigms are fundamentally insufficient for ensuring the integrity of automated research. We further propose mitigation strategies and demonstrate that access to full workflow artifacts (log traces and code) enables more effective auditing. Our findings suggest that journals, conferences, and researchers should move beyond manuscript-only evaluation toward process auditing the end-to-end workflow artifacts of AI scientist systems.\", \"doi\": \"10.1073/pnas.2610214123\", \"pmid\": \"42832657\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13663820\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2610214123\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13663820\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13663820?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Autonomous AI research agents in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma immunology: from multimod…

We further propose mitigation strategies and demonstrate that access to full workflow artifacts (log traces and code) enables more effective auditing. Our findings suggest that journals, conferences, and researchers should move beyond manuscript-only evaluation toward process auditing the end-to-end workflow artifacts of AI scientist systems.\", \"doi\": \"10.1073/pnas.2610214123\", \"pmid\": \"42832657\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13663820\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.2610214123\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13663820\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13663820?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"Autonomous AI research agents in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma immunology: from multimodal evidence to experimental validation.\", \"abstract\": \"Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the most challenging malignancies due to profound biological heterogeneity, complex stromal organization, and limited responsiveness to current immunotherapies. Recent advances in single-cell sequencing, spatial omics, digital pathology, and multimodal profiling have revealed that PDAC immune states are shaped not only by cellular composition but also by spatial organization, treatment context, and patient-specific evolutionary trajectories. However, the increasing complexity and fragmentation of biomedical evidence create substantial challenges for conventional artificial intelligence (AI) approaches that are typically optimized for predefined analytical tasks. Autonomous AI research agents represent an emerging paradigm that extends beyond predictive modeling by integrating scientific reasoning, retrieval of heterogeneous biomedical knowledge, computational tool orchestration, workflow adaptation, and evidence traceability. In this Review, we examine how agentic AI systems may contribute to PDAC immunology research, from characterization of immune ecosystems and spatial cellular interactions to biomarker discovery, neoantigen prioritization, and experimental protocol design. We distinguish AI agents from conventional task-specific models and discuss essential capabilities required for reliable biomedical research, including planning, tool use, verification, memory, provenance tracking, and human oversight. Despite promising technical demonstrations in biomedical domains, direct evidence supporting fully autonomous AI-driven discovery and validation in PDAC remains limited. Therefore, we propose a disease-oriented evaluation framework emphasizing benchmark task design, appropriate human and computational comparators, reproducibility assessment, and experimental validation. Future PDAC-specific AI research agents should prioritize evidence-aware reasoning, multimodal integration, calibrated uncertainty, and transparent computational-experimental workflows. Such systems may ultimately accelerate mechanistic discovery and precision immunology, while maintaining rigorous standards for biological validity, reproducibility, and responsible scientific practice.\", \"doi\": \"10.3389/fimmu.2026.1983838\", \"pmid\": \"42921155\", \"pmcid\": \"PMC13691739\", \"source\": \"MED\", \"fullTextUrlList\": {\"fullTextUrl\": [{\"availability\": \"Subscription required\", \"availabilityCode\": \"S\", \"documentStyle\": \"doi\", \"site\": \"DOI\", \"url\": \"https://doi.org/10.3389/fimmu.2026.1983838\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"html\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13691739\"}, {\"availability\": \"Open access\", \"availabilityCode\": \"OA\", \"documentStyle\": \"pdf\", \"site\": \"Europe_PMC\", \"url\": \"https://europepmc.org/articles/PMC13691739?pdf=render\"}]}}, {\"title\": \"From existence checking to semantic auditing: citation verifiability in the age of AI.\", \"abstract\": \"This paper reflects on the current crisis of academic integrity caused by the phenomenon of fabricated and semantically incorrect citations. In the era of 'fast science' and permanent citation inflation, human reviewers face extreme cognitive overload and time pressure, making it impossible to consistently verify literature sources. As a key solution, this paper proposes the deployment of autonomous AI agents (Agentic AI) designed for the deep semantic auditing of manuscripts. This technological shift is complemented by an innovative proposal to introduce mandatory authorial 'citation reports' that operationalize the concepts of citation classification. The resulting synergy between human expertise and machine precision relieves reviewers of their mechanical burden and can help strengthen the rigor, transparency, and credibility of peer review.\",
